thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate on /v1/generate across us-east-1 (90s aggregation) — error_rate=11.8% · paging @Erin (oncall) · incident severity: P1
Erin: ack, looking. where are metrics & logs?
Maya: I'm on it, checking runtime dashboards now (model-runner).
Erin: rough scope: top-level 5xx + timeouts reported by gateway, some customers are seeing complete failures. any recent deploys?
Sanjay: no user-facing deploys in last 3 hours. infra autoscaler had a config tweak yesterday but nothing since.
Maya: grabbing pod logs. preliminary: repeated segfaults in model-runner pods, error pattern: "double free" not obvious but kernel OOM a possibility. tail below:
```
model-runner[pid=2478]: INFO start inference model=redwood-v1 qtype=quant8
model-runner[pid=2478]: WARN kv-cache miss for session=abc123
model-runner[pid=2478]: ERROR runtime: segfault at 0x0 ip=0x7f8a3b2c1234 sp=0x7ffe... pc=0x7f8a3b2c1234
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation]
goroutine 52 [running]:
runtime.throw(0x8b2a1d, 0x2a)
	/usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:1112 +0x72
runtime.sigpanic()
	/usr/local/go/src/runtime/signal_unix.go:718 +0x3e4
```
Erin: ugh. Maya can you confirm whether it's a user-requested sequence that triggers it or random? Also hit counts / per-model stats.
Maya: crash loop in 3 pods: model-runner-0, model-runner-4, model-runner-9. OOM not reported in dmesg, just segfault. libattention.so referenced in stack traces. Hash of last container image: sha256:9f1a... (pinned to redwood/v1-2026-03-04)
Maya: running `kubectl describe pod model-runner-4 -n inference` now.
Sanjay: routing layer shows fallback to gateway 502 for requests to model=redwood-v1. Traffic is backed up to gateway-proxy queues, latency spiking.
James: starting immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert new traffic from redwood-v1 to redwood-v1-fallback (smaller non-quantized variant), 2) scale up fallback pool, 3) pull affected pods out of LB.
Erin: prioritize: minimize customer error rate first. do the traffic change. @Maya can you push routing rule?
Maya: applying route rewrite now. command: `rbctl routes set --model redwood-v1 --fallback redwood-v1-fallback --percent 100 --region us-east-1`
Maya: route applied. Confirming traffic shift... gateway logs show redwood-v1 request rate -> 2% now, fallback -> 98%. error_rate on /v1/generate dropping in 2m window from 11.8% -> 2.1%. :+1:
Support Ops: support queue showing major incidents for 6 customers (Acme, Finovate, StudyAI...). Sent initial status update to affected customers and page to enterprise contacts.
Erin: good. next: remove affected pods so they stop crashing & consuming memory. Maya, can you cordon/drain the nodes with the crashing pods?
Maya: cordoning node gke-infer-13, draining pods. Note: one of the pods had a very high RSS ~48GB before crash (model size ~40GB). possible memory leak with certain request shapes.
Sanjay: I'll add a temporary circuit-break at gateway to limit concurrent requests per-session to 4 for us-east to reduce pressure on models. applying now.
James: also enabling a config flip to force non-quant kernels on redwood-v1-fallback to avoid kernel-level bug in quantized path. Patch deployed to runtime-config: `inference.runtime.force_scalar_kernels=true`
Maya: live logs show segfaults stopping; we have healthy fallback pool handling traffic. error_rate down to 0.8% across region.
Erin: nice work. let's capture root cause evidence. Maya, collect full core dumps and stack traces from the crashed pods (if present) and upload to the incident bucket. include container image sha, model weights hash, recent kernel modules.
Maya: starting core dump collection: command snippet for reproducibility:
```
kubectl cp inference/model-runner-4:/var/crash/core.2478 ./core.2478
aws s3 cp ./core.2478 s3://redwood-incidents/1758004321/
```
Maya: note — cores are ~1.2GB each. uploading, ETA ~6m.
Support Ops: customer-facing status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1758004321 — summary posted. Sent mail to SL contacts at 16:14 UTC.
Erin: assessing blast radius: traffic profile shows 14% of total hosted API calls touched redwood-v1 this window; most traffic now on fallback. Top 3 customers saw 20-40% of their traffic affected. No data exfiltration.
James: we should also roll model-runner image to previous known-good image to be safe. scheduling rolling restart with image `redwood/v1-2026-02-20` on drained nodes only.
Maya: performing canary restart on one node with older image, running health checks (latency p50/p95, error rate).
Maya: canary looks stable for 8m. no segfaults.
Erin: ok plan: 1) keep fallback route at 100% for 20m, 2) rollback model-runner on drained nodes to older image, 3) after 30m observe, gradually swing traffic back to primary if stable, 4) collect artifacts for postmortem.
Sanjay: added a temporary metric alert to detect segfault rate (logs matching "SIGSEGV") so we get faster pages if this recurs.
Liz: hi — I'm taking handoff at 16:45 UTC. Summary: segfaults in model-runner for redwood-v1 caused elevated 5xx; we diverted all traffic to fallback, scaled fallback, drained nodes, started image rollback; error rate reduced to <1%. core dumps and stacks collected. ongoing: finish rolling restart and run extended validation. I'll follow up with timeline and RCA notes.
Erin: thanks Liz, appreciate the pickup. I will be available for questions.
Liz: will open incident ticket and assign owners: RCA -> Maya, runtime patch / kernel investigation -> James, customer comms -> Support Ops. Will also tag security and compliance for review (no evidence of data leakage).
Support Ops: note — two enterprise customers requested credits and resumed degraded traffic; handled via existing CX playbook.
Maya: uploaded core dumps and logs to s3://redwood-incidents/1758004321/ and linked in ticket. Also included `strace` of a reproducer attempt on canary.
James: quick analysis: stack samples show crash in quantized attention kernel path; hypothesis: a refcount bug in custom CUDA kernel when handling zero-length prefix in KV cache. starting unit test to reproduce.
Erin: good hypothesis. if confirmed, we'll need a patch to kernel and a minor runtime release; meanwhile plan to keep fallback config that avoids quant kernels.
Liz: posting current status update to channel and updating incident ticket with next steps and ETA for full rollback completion ~16:55 UTC.
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: handoff from Erin to Liz at 16:45 UTC. Incident status: mitigation in progress, customer impact reduced.
Erin: adding action items for postmortem: 1) reproduce locally and write unit test for KV prefix handling (owner: James), 2) improve prod-safe routing playbook to allow faster 1-click fallback (owner: Maya), 3) validate memory accounting for heavy sessions and add quota (owner: Sanjay), 4) customer follow-up & credits (owner: Support Ops).
Liz: will schedule postmortem meeting and assign JIRA RD-1758004321. Closing note: current customer-facing status indicates "degraded" and will move to "resolved" after final validation.
Support Ops: thanks team — customers appreciating quick response. closing alert once rollouts finish. :white_check_mark:
Erin: thanks everyone. I'll mark this as triaged; please paste final incident summary into the ticket when done.
